title: bromus tectorum subsp. longipilus
intro: Bromus tectorum subsp. longipilus, commonly known as cheatgrass, is a subspecies of the Cheatgrass plant. It is a type of grass that is native to North America and has been widely naturalized across various regions. The plant has been found to have several health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, which can be attributed to its therapeutic actions of reducing inflammation and fighting off infections. The bioactive constituents of cheatgrass include sesquiterpenes, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties and potential uses in traditional medicine.
